en: My forefather is the hero Manas,
My leopard father is Semetey,
And I am Seytek, son of Semetey—
My armored host numbers eighty-four,
What I strike flares into red fire.
My homeland is broad Talas,
My grandfather is grey-maned brave Manas.
If you pitch your royal camp, that is the land;
If you seek a husband, that is the man.
Seek Seytek, your equal,
If you suffer and set out on the road,
The Creator will grant your desire.
You will attain your aim;
If you do not seek him,
Your tiny soul will cry out,
And all your bones will ache.
You will see many hardships;
Burning in soul and crying Seytek,
You will waste away with longing.
The true place from which none return,
You will see all too soon.
Having said this, the four champions
Vanished from sight,
And my breast filled with light.
We plunged into delight,
Promising a joyful night,
We lay rejoicing together.
When we entered the greatest delight,
Seytek and I together,
Alas for that play and pleasure,
It was a dream without truth.
Grief came from the unseen;
When pale dawn spread,
The eastern sky grew bright,
And I awoke from sleep.
The hero who lay in my embrace was gone;
Such filth is this world.
It was as if he had transformed and vanished.
God Most High creates souls
In every different fashion.
To take my own dark life,
What could I do? My hand would not act.
Burning, I became an ember;
Fuming, I became fire.
Unable to take my own life,
I stopped close to death.
In the time it takes to open and close my eyes,
Parted from my splendid hero,
Grief stirred within me.
The moon turned pale in the sky;
Parted from my lion hero,
Regret stirred within me.
Unable to endure this world—
Thus she cried out,
And spoke while sobbing.
Her soul-companion Kulayim—
Her confidante who untied every knot,
The radiant hapless maiden's
Companion sharing even death,
Who walked and stood together with her,
Her companion of one desire.
I sing and tell my song,
I faithfully tell my secret.
My heart becomes flame and embers.
Bearing my longing for Seytek,
While alive, my soul has grieved;
From my royal throne,
I have been parted from my city.
My heart burned in flames,
And my arms became like dry reeds.
If I blink and see a dream,
And lie once to satisfy my longing,
When I sleep, I am together with him;
When I wake, he is not beside me.
I burn from this affliction,
Yellowing, I lament and grieve.
When the leopard comes to mind,
Friend Kulayim, hear my words:
When I slept at night and dreamed,
When I saw a wondrous thing in my dream,
The sign of the dream I saw was this—
Had surrounded me.
What can this mean?
Interpret this dream of mine.
At the very core of my heart,
They came together and sank within.
I held the sun in my right hand,
And held the moon in my left.
I plunged into this wonder,
Until my beloved returned from his journey,
I held them, saying, I need you,
And lay wrestling and playing.
What can this mean?
Again I saw a marvel,
Most wondrous when I ponder it.
From an unknown place there came
Twelve blades of keen steel,
And these treasures were found for me.
That fitting, precious sharp blade
Fell into my right hand.
The black stone opposite split apart.
The twelve steel blades were strong;
Wherever they swung became fire.
What can this mean?
Interpret this dream of mine.
I have another wonder;
My dear companion, hear it.
From out of nowhere there came
A wild saker falcon that would not perch on a hand,
And its tether wrapped around my waist.
That saker falcon of mine
Had a vast, sweeping stride,
Its sides stretched broadly in every direction.
Its black-steel talons
Made blood rain wherever they seized.
I perched it upon my hand,
Mounted a chestnut horse,
And donned a costly silk robe.
I removed its hood.
With a full complement of fierce weapons,
I raised an uproar.
I sent it against lions and bears,
And split open their bellies.
Their devices exhausted, cried out;
Scattered and shattered apart.
It crushed whatever it pursued,
And defeated whatever resisted.
Those that fled to escape it
Died when their hearts failed.
This is the peerless champion, they said;
May your bird be auspicious, they said.
The white-bearded ishan sobbed,
Giving me their blessing.
Every animal and living creature,
I bound it firmly on my right side,
And kept it overnight on my perch.
I saw such a champion bird.
Had fortified herself thus,
Exercising wisdom and devising plans,
All the champions gathered around,
The guards could not approach him face to face.
Over on this side, to [Perishte],
Her guard could not deliver the news.
The figures of [the servants],
All fully equipped,
Each one carried a spear.
The guard standing watch,
Dazed and bewildered,
They have seen his true might.
They rode arrow-swift steeds.
Every one carried a steel spear.
They cast no glance upon the world.
The mortal upon whom they cast their gaze
The excellent giver of counsel—
My God has opened your fortune.
Attend to my answer, [elder sister].
As I observe, this is their nature.
They level everything they advance upon.
No human can stand before him.
Such is his heroism.
No one can stand facing him.
He has arranged his seven weapons.
Such is his lion-like strength.
He is a handsome, fierce, lion-like warrior.
He is fierce; he is a hero.
She dressed, choosing the most precious garments.
My heart has surged open with joy.
A blessed night has come to my fate.
Companions who walk beside me,
Beauties as lovely as paradise,
The beholder's attention is captivated.
Having captivated those who saw her,
Was amazed, his attention captivated.
[Imploring], saying, Let me see her again,
All of them companions of equal standing,
They bustled with all their strength.
Mind was overcome with wonder.
Her broad bosom and chest,
Delicate Crimean soft boots,
See the pearls, then see her teeth.
See the hare, then see her back.
[Prancing proudly], [flashing], swaying lightly,
God Most High, the Almighty,
The wide world had become narrow
They pledged a white-headed sheep.
Was [covered like ash].
Waiting for lionlike Seytek to come,
Akjoltoy appeared as her destined husband;
Turning gracefully like a doe,
We set our expedition upon the road,
And wrestlers who blocked our path
Akbermet and Seytek, the two lovers.
Or is this today's new custom?
My lion Joltoy, heed what I say.
We bow our heads before you,
Hear my words, my lord Seytek.
Such is our condition.
My omen stirred, my eyes flashed.
Great blessing and prosperity will be found for you.
Two fairy maidens will come to you.
The pillow filled with swan [down]
Was placed beneath their elbows.
Beside Akbermet and Ayım,
Warrior Seytek and Akjoltoy,
Sighing and shifting about,
The noblemen lay stretched out.
Six beautiful maidens served the food.
Listen closely to this account.
They set tea in the large teapot,
And set out each kind of food.
Golden bowls and copper platters
They brought and rinsed.
They placed honey beside the liquor.
Slicing [bread], slicing, they set out bread.
They sliced horse-rump meat and set out neck fat.
They hastened to boil the tea.
They spread and filled the dining cloth.
They warmed them with fermented mare's milk,
And heated them with liquor.
Akbermet and Külayım,
Since God had granted their wish,
Since the one they awaited had come,
Remained standing upright,
To leopard-like Seytek and Joltoy,
Bowing as they offered bowls.
Looking at the extraordinary merriment,
There were all manner of entertainments.
Among the beauties,
What was there, and what was missing?
Shouts rose in a great uproar,
A clamor that split the sky.
A copper cauldron with six handles
They brought and set over the fire.
Of horse-belly fat thick as a sole,
And innards, they had portions put in.
Her known purpose was this.
Had she not brought it along?
When your hero Seytek arrived,
Thanks to your hero Seytek,
[Uncertain: this was …]
Who met the Night of Power.
The people's wish, for the nation,
The leopard-like hero protecting the people.
The blessing given [to the people?],
The lion, his [venerable forefather?],
Who cared for these dear people.
Worthy and patient,
[Worthy?] in every disposition.
The wise among the Kyrgyz,
The brave Kulchu, who knew the circumstances.
The fool who knew nothing,
Made equal with the people's sons,
One person from each group,
Their forefather, their mainstay,
See his valor.
Great and small, old and young,
